title: Counting Bits
prompt:
Count the number of 1-bits for every integer from 0 to n using dynamic programming in `solution.ts`.

**Approach:**
Build a DP array where `dp[i]` stores the number of 1-bits in the binary representation of `i`. Use the recurrence `dp[i] = dp[i >> 1] + (i & 1)`. The key insight: right-shifting `i` by 1 removes the last bit, and `i & 1` tells you what that last bit was. So the popcount of `i` is the popcount of `i / 2` (floored) plus the last bit.

**Requirements:**
1. Export `countBits(n: number): number[]` -- takes a non-negative integer `n` and returns an array of length `n + 1` where element `i` is the number of 1-bits in the binary representation of `i`
2. Use a `for` loop from 1 to n
3. Use the bit-shift DP recurrence: `dp[i] = dp[i >> 1] + (i & 1)`

**Examples:**
```typescript
countBits(2)  // [0, 1, 1]
countBits(5)  // [0, 1, 1, 2, 1, 2]
countBits(0)  // [0]
```

**Complexity:** O(n) time, O(n) space.
hints: Initialize dp as an array of n + 1 zeros: new Array(n + 1).fill(0)
i >> 1 is the same as Math.floor(i / 2) (right shift removes the last bit)
i & 1 extracts the least significant bit (0 or 1)
dp[0] = 0 is the base case (zero has no 1-bits)

solution.ts.name: countBits
solution.ts.description: Export countBits as a named export
Use a for loop to build the DP array
